description:
Dispatcher for note operations: create, render, edit, query. Almost entirely interactive.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it for editing (INTERACTIVE)
  copy [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents into a new note at the current timestamp (INTERACTIVE)
  strip [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents and remove the body, for templating (INTERACTIVE)
  edit [FILTER] — pick a note, open in the default editor (INTERACTIVE)
  nano [FILTER] — pick a note, open in nano (INTERACTIVE)
  last — open the most recently-created note; the only non-interactive subcommand
  delete [FILTER] — pick a note and permanently delete it (INTERACTIVE, DESTRUCTIVE)
  cat [FILTER] — pick a note and print it to stdout (INTERACTIVE)
  pdf [FILTER] — pick a note, render PDF plus markdown to the export directory (INTERACTIVE)
  minutes [FILTER] — pick a note, render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (INTERACTIVE)
  agenda [FILTER] — pick a note, render a meeting agenda (INTERACTIVE)

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — optional; with no subcommand the tool runs `new`.
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring narrowing the picker list.

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except `last` opens a picker and reads a selection from stdin. With no terminal it consumes EOF and behaves unpredictably rather than erroring. Call only ["last"]. Never call new, copy, strip, edit, nano, delete, cat, pdf, minutes or agenda, and never call with an empty argv (that runs `new`).
  To find and read notes without a picker, use `search notes` for paths and read the file directly.
  Note bodies use keyword lines: ACTION: (ingested by `tasks`), TASK: (written by `tasks`, never by hand), AGREED:, RESOLVED:, !: (important callout).
  pdf, minutes and agenda need pandoc and a LaTeX engine.

BLOCKED: new, copy, strip, edit, nano, last, delete, cat, pdf, minutes, agenda. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
